about: Entries for CPUIDs the article has no row for, each fact with the page it came from. import.py appends them after the article's and refuses one whose CPUID the article has: the article's own row is kept. Its models are those whose ARK ordering tab gives D2, Q0 or J1; ARK no longer has pages for the Sandy Bridge Pentium and Celeron parts: they are listed, with their codes, from the identification tables of the same specification updates (324827, 324643), the brand from the document's own text or, for G460, G622 and G632, which it names by number only, from Wikipedia's lists. Intel's specification updates for the mobile and desktop parts (324827, 324643; Intel no longer serves them, the URLs are web.archive.org copies of its own) give every row, D-2, J-1 and Q-0, the signature 000206a7h: so J1, the dual-core die, is this CPUID's too.
